title: Hardy and Cabello Arguments in Spatial and Temporal Frauchiger-Renner Scenarios
authors: Ehsan Erfani Maharat, Ali Ahanj, Mohsen Sarbishaei
abstract: We investigate Hardy- and Cabello-type logical structures within spatial and temporal extensions of the Frauchiger--Renner (FR) framework, embedding these constructions directly into the FR multi-observer architecture. In the spatial multi-observer scenario, both Hardy and Cabello contradictions arise, with the Cabello construction yielding the stronger violation,$\(Δ_{\rm Cabello}^{\max}=0.1078\)$, which exceeds the maximal Hardy probability $\(P_{H}^{\max}=\frac{5\sqrt{5}-11}{2}\approx 0.09017\)$. We then develop a sequential temporal FR protocol based on coherent multi-observer measurements performed on a single spin-$\tfrac12$ system. In this temporal setting, the Hardy contradiction disappears identically due to dynamical constraints imposed by sequential state updates, whereas a finite Cabello-type violation survives, \(Δ_{\rm Cabello}^{\max}\approx 0.0674\). Our results establish a fundamental structural distinction between spatial entanglement and temporal multi-observer correlations in FR-type logical scenarios, and demonstrate that certain observer-independent description failures persist even without spacelike separation.
summary: The paper analyzes Hardy and Cabello paradoxes in both spatial and temporal extensions of the Frauchiger–Renner framework. It demonstrates that while the strong Hardy contradiction disappears in sequential time measurements, a weaker nonclassical tension (Cabello violation) persists. This highlights how measurement structure fundamentally dictates the type and strength of quantum correlations observed.
main_problem: The study investigates Hardy- and Cabello-type logical structures within extensions of the Frauchiger–Renner (FR) framework to distinguish between quantum correlations in spatial versus temporal measurement settings.
main_result: The analysis shows that while the strong Hardy contradiction vanishes identically in the sequential temporal protocol due to state update constraints, a weaker but persistent Cabello-type violation remains. This establishes a fundamental structural difference between spatial and temporal nonlocality witnesses.
method: The authors use quantum probability theory to calculate joint measurement probabilities for multi-observer scenarios, optimizing quantities like $\Delta_{	ext{Cabello}}$ subject to zero-probability constraints derived from the Hardy paradox structure.
model_or_system: The model is a reformulation of the FR thought experiment applied to a single spin-1/2 system undergoing sequential projective measurements by multiple observers (Alice, Bob, Charlie, Debbie) over time. The analysis compares this temporal setting to its spatially separated counterpart.
key_observables: Hardy contradiction probability ($P_H$), Cabello violation parameter ($\Delta_{	ext{Cabello}}$), and joint measurement probabilities $P(A, B)$, $P(C, D)$.

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes ideal projective measurements, unitary evolution between measurement stages, and relies on comparing the structural constraints imposed by zero-probability assumptions.

paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the Hardy and Cabello arguments first in a spatial multi-observer context, establishing quantitative bounds. It then extends this formalism to a sequential temporal protocol, demonstrating how dynamical constraints alter the nature and strength of the observed nonclassicality.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it probes the limits of quantum correlations under realistic physical assumptions (like time evolution), providing theoretical tools to distinguish between different forms of contextuality beyond simple Bell tests.
